s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive scalp mass with ulceration and bleeding, associated with cervical lymphadenopathy and suspected distant metastases
salient_findings: Ulceration and easy bleeding of the mass
key_facts: 10-year history of right-sided scalp mass
Mass was stable and nontender until excision 5 months ago
Mass recurred, enlarged, ulcerated, and bled easily after excision
Patient denied headaches, convulsions, or neurologic deficits
Patient was afebrile and hemodynamically stable
No pallor, jaundice, or palpable peripheral lymphadenopathy
Two lesions on the right side of the scalp
Laboratory studies showed normal complete blood count and basic metabolic panel
Chest radiography and abdominal/pelvic ultrasound were unremarkable
Head and neck CT scan showed multilobulated, hyperdense, ulcerative right frontal scalp lesion
MRI of the spine revealed pathological compression fracture of T10 and hyperintense lesion in T8

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: most common cause of scalp masses with ulceration and bleeding

shortlist.label: Basal cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: common skin cancer that can cause scalp masses

shortlist.label: Merkel cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: aggressive skin cancer that can cause scalp masses and metastases

shortlist.label: Angiosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: rare but aggressive cancer that can cause scalp masses and bleeding

shortlist.label: Metastatic carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: possible cause of multiple lesions and distant metastases

raw.rationale: The patient's 10-year history of a stable scalp mass that became aggressive after excision, along with the presence of a fungating, tender, and bleeding mass, and the imaging findings of a multilobulated, hyperdense, ulcerative lesion, are consistent with squamous cell carcinoma, a common skin cancer that can be locally aggressive and metastasize.

rejected.label: Basal cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Typically less aggressive and less likely to metastasize

rejected.label: Merkel cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Usually has a more rapid onset and is more aggressive, but the 10-year history does not support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Angiosarcoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with a more rapid onset and is often associated with lymphedema or radiation exposure, which is not mentioned in the case

rejected.label: Metastatic carcinoma
rejected.why: The primary site of the cancer is likely the scalp, given the long history of the mass, rather than a metastasis from another site
